description:
Invoking `Activity#reportFullyDrawn()` once the data has been loaded and the screen has been rendered to the user.

The entry points into the app are the OnboardingActivity, MainActivity, and SessionDetailsActvitiy. Each of these report when they have been fully drawn independently to the framework. The Android framework prints a log statement as follows:
```
I/ActivityTaskManager: Fully drawn com.google.samples.apps.iosched/.ui.MainActivity: +3s493ms
```
This is used for measuring startup time and is a helpful signal when diagnosing startup performance issues. Check out the [vitals documentation](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/vitals/launch-time#time-full) for more about the usage of `reportFullyDrawn()`.

comments.body:
Will `.lastPathSegment` capture `sessions` by mistake (instead of the id) if the URI is of the form `iosched://sessions?session_id={id}`?

In any case this might be better as a separate change if there's a bug with the current code here.
You could alternatively have this class implement `ThemedActivityDelegate` so that the activity only needs one ViewModel (as in `MainActivityViewModel`). I have no strong opinion on it either way.
OnboardingActivity doesn't gate `reportFullyDrawn()` with `doOnLayout` or similar, so I wonder if this will report too soon (the view is created, but is it actually shown yet?)

Good point! I'll revert this piece. I am not sure if there is a bug because alarm manager seems to send the intent with query params but I could not get the query params to work through adb so there is some magic happening somewhere. Let's assume it is working but if it is not, then we can create a bug and fix it outside of the scope of this change.

I assumed that the view was already completed at this point since it is hard coded data in the view. Just to be safe, I am adding `doOnLayout` just in case there is still some measuring happening. I assume the difference in start up time would be negligible.
Per your overall comment, by calling the method on the activity directly, there is no longer a need for these viewmodels. Marking as resolved since this is no longer relevant.
Nope, I am surprised the CI checks didn't catch this. I thought I had organized imports before committing but evidently I didn't. 😅
